surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of Sr(thd)2 and Ti(O–iPr)2(thd)2 precursors followed by a water pulse to regenerate OH sites. The crystallization of the seed layer and the main layer STO films is influenced by the annealing temperature and the interfacial interactions between the STO seed and Ru electrode. The in situ crystallization of the main layer STO is facilitated by a crystallized seed layer, and the chemical interactions between the seed layer and the Ru electrode can inhibit crystallization.
evidence: The text discusses the influence of the annealing temperature on the crystallization of the seed layer and the main layer STO films. It mentions the formation of a SRO phase due to chemical interactions between the STO seed and Ru electrode, and the presence of amorphous STO regions due to incomplete crystallization. The surface reaction mechanism is described in the context of the adsorption of Sr(thd)2 and Ti(O–iPr)2(thd)2 precursors and the water pulse to regenerate OH sites.
